{{Quote|The cave is collapsing!''"<br />"''This is no cave.|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="ESB" />}}
The '''exogorth''', colloquially known as the '''space slug''', was a gigantic [[Silicon/Legends|silicon]]-based<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> [[Species/Legends|species]] of toothed [[Gastropod/Legends|gastropod]] that survived in the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] by making their homes in the caverns and craters of [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]]. They fed on the minerals of asteroids, various stellar energy fields, [[Mynock/Legends|mynocks]], ships, and other unfortunate creatures that unknowingly passed into its [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]]. 

==Biology==
[[File:SpaceSlug.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An exogorth]]
The average adult space slug grew to about 10 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length;<ref name="SWCE" /> however, there had been instances of near-[[Kilometer/Legends|kilometer]]-long specimens.<ref name="SWCE" /> Space slugs also molted as a result of their growth.<ref name="DS">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref> Occasionally, this mechanism would be overridden, and the slug would grow to monstrous sizes.<ref name="HNN54">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|54|life/1352_2.html|Giant Space Slug Found}}</ref>

A space slug would travel through the [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belts]] they inhabited by pushing off the surface of one [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] and floating through [[Realspace/Legends|space]] to land on another. They also could use stellar winds to help propel themselves through space.<ref name="KOTOR 19">[[Knights of the Old Republic 19|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 19]]</ref> Through highly evolved sense of spatial awareness, they were capable of calculating the speed, trajectory, and distance of perilous moving bodies around them. This sense of spatial acuity also aided them in hunting food. They appeared to have been able to anchor themselves into a cave in an asteroid with tendrils, which also drew nutrition directly from the asteroid itself.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide" /> As a space slug did not remain in one asteroid for its entire life, it can be assumed that they could break free from their point of anchorage without causing significant injury to themselves. Although their primary diet, similar to [[Mynock/Legends|mynocks]], was passive radiation, they did tend to chomp on rocks and metal as well.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

[[File:SpaceslugAnat-woswfg.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Anatomy of the giant exogorth]]

On occasion, the naturally occurring chemical trigger would cause the space slug to kill whatever occurred near them. These oddities were known to reach sizes of nearly one kilometer in length. These colossal slugs were known to take sizable bites out of [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] that passed too close to the slug's current dwelling, and even swallow smaller vessels whole. At these sizes, the mynocks they ate would often become internal parasites, rather than nourishment, living inside the cave-like esophagus of the slugs that ate them. Some slugs had entire ecosystems of other life living within their digestive tracts.

The [[Cularin space slug]] variety of exogorth [[Reproduction/Legends|reproduced]] via fission, whereby a slug that attained a sufficiently large size would divide into two smaller space slugs.<ref name="Cularin Space Slug">{{Wizards|url=starwars/article.asp?x=sw20010426c_slug&c=rpg|series=Creature Feature|text=Cularin Space Slug}}</ref>

A natural predator of the space slug was the [[Colossus wasp/Legends|colossus wasp]].

===Exogorth variations===
[[File:Crimsonslug-TSIA.jpg|thumb|left|125px|[[Crimson slug]]s]]
A number of space slug variations existed, such as the giant slug, the [[crimson slug]]s, and the Cularin slugs. Giant space slugs were larger than average ones. It remains unclear if they were a separate species from the common space slug, or just individuals larger than normally reported.<ref name="Smart">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20020919slug|series=Creature Feature|text=Smart Space Slug}}</ref>

Crimson slugs were a species of space slug native to the asteroids of [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]]. They were distinguished by a red stripe down either side of the body.<ref name="TSIA">''[[Tapani Sector Instant Adventures]]''</ref>

Cularin space slugs were a variety of exogorth found in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]] which proved to be comparatively easy to train. Some theorized that they were descended from a domesticated creatures. Other theories held that these exogorths were descended from natives to the world which formed the [[Cularin asteroid belt]] ([[Oblis]]) before its [[Destruction of Oblis|destruction]], and that these creatures survived and adapted to the void of space.<ref name="Cularin Space Slug" /> They may have been related to&mdash;or the same creature as&mdash;the [[Space worm/Legends|space worms]] which hollowed out the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Eskaron]].

==History==
{{Quote|They're the last remnant of a species that predates history&mdash;an unlikely being, if ever there was one. No one knows how or why they evolved&mdash;just that we have found a number of them in the galaxy, going about their business&hellip;Time has no meaning for such a creature&hellip;We thought for a time that they might have once been plentiful in the galaxy&mdash;and the ones we find now are the only ones left.|[[Arkoh Adasca]]|<ref name="kotor18">[[Knights of the Old Republic 18|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 18]]</ref>}}
Exogorths were commonly [[Hunting/Legends|hunted]] by [[slug hunter]]s, who sought the creatures' skin and organs. Slug hunters would spend weeks on end exploring asteroid fields for slugs to target and would typically slay the leviathans by entering their mouths and opening fire with [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] weapons. One group of hunters used such tactics on the the intelligent space slug [[Turmok]], who shut its mouth and shook its attackers to [[Death/Legends|death]]. Turmok subsequently captured the hunters' [[Starship/Legends|starship]] and kept the vessel its mouth for further study.<ref name="Smart" />

[[File:KotOR21-FC.png|thumb|right|180px|An exogorth attacks [[The Last Resort (starship)|''The Last Resort'']] in [[3963 BBY]].]]
The [[House of Adasca]] found a way to control the slugs, known to [[The Adasca BioMechanical Corporation of Arkania|Adascorp]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] as exogorths, after the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. Based on the research of [[Gorman Vandrayk]], Adascorp was able to control the hunger drives, growth rate, and reproductive fission processes of the creatures. [[Arkoh Adasca]] placed control mechanisms and [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] engines on a group of slugs and sought to sell them to the Republic, the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], or the [[Revanchist]] faction as [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]]. With the Adascorp modifications, the exogorths could be sent through hyperspace to a specific system. Once there, their increased rate of growth and division could lead to destruction of space stations, asteroids, moons, and possibly even planets. The original exogorths could be sent to another system once they had divided, making it possible to disrupt or destroy hundreds of systems in a very short time. None of the parties who were invited to bid on these new weapons were enthusiastic about using them, however, all three were interested in making sure the weapon did not fall into the other parties' hands. Camper was able to escape and used the exogorths to kill Adasca atop of the ''[[Arkanian Legacy]]''{{'s}} bridge and then lure them out to [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].

[[File:Spaceslug_swk.jpg|thumb|left|150px|An exogorth trying to swallow the ''Millennium Falcon'']]

Thousands of years later, the notorious [[Mugaari]] pirate [[Clabburn the Elder]] seeded the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]] with space slugs, in order to protect his hidden smuggler bases.<ref name="ISW">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> In one recorded occurrence a slug living in that asteroid field grew to a size of about 900 meters in length. It was found and officially recorded by [[Gamgalon]] the [[Krish (species)/Legends|Krish]], who made a living by capturing these massive specimens.<ref name="EGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>

One 80-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long specimen was observed by the [[University of Sanbra]] in the [[Borkeen Belt]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. This space slug made [[HoloNet News/Legends|headlines]], as it was the largest ever found by the university.<ref name="HNN54" />

A juvenile space slug lived on [[Ostfrei]], a moon of the Cularin system planet [[Genarius]], during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The creature was encountered by a group of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance]] agents sent by the [[Senator/Legends|senatorial]] [[Aide/Legends|aide]] [[Sa'arli]] to investigate reports of suspiscious activity on Ostfrei.<ref name="Who Goes Thare?">{{LivingForce|Who Goes Thaere?}}</ref>

During the [[Galactic War]], the lair of a [[Minos Cluster exogorth|rare exogorth]] was found in the [[Minos Cluster/Legends|Minos Cluster]]. Upon being investigated, the worm was just shedding its valuable skin, and several pieces of it were retrieved for studying.<ref name="TBotW">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Bioanalysis|The Belly of the Worm}}</ref>

The asteroid belt in the [[Algunnis system/Legends|Algunnis system]] of the [[Trax sector/Legends|Trax sector]] was home to several huge exogorths.<ref name="GK">''[[Star Wars Gamemaster Kit]]''</ref>

[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] unwittingly hid the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] in a space slug of similar size when running from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. Since exogorths insulated themselves deep inside asteroids and their own heat-generating waste, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], Han Solo, and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] were able to survive inside the space slug with only [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]] to provide [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]]. Solo had heard stories for years of the giant slugs, and had been warned of their dangers, but he dismissed them as mere "ghost stories."<ref name="ESB" />

Certain facilities that resided in space kept a space slug living close by to help keep the pesky mynock population down. To keep these specially used slugs from reproducing and growing to uncontrollable sizes, [[katrium]] was introduced into the creature's system on a regular basis.

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Once again, Lucas has woven into the story the imagery of consumption and of the journey into the belly of the beast&hellip;Han, Leia, Chewie, and See-Threepio have been swallowed whole, just as Jonah was swallowed by the whale.|[[Mary Henderson]], author of ''Star Wars: The Magic of Myth''|<ref name="magic of myth">''[[Star Wars: The Magic of Myth]]''</ref>}}
[[File:MCQ-spaceslug.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Ralph McQuarrie concept art of a space slug]]
A single exogorth first appeared in [[1980]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], the second film in the [[original trilogy]],<ref name="ESB" /> but was known simply as a space slug<ref name="db">{{DB|creature|spaceslug|space slug}}</ref> until [[2007]], when [[Knights of the Old Republic 18|the eighteenth issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (comic series)|''Knights of the Old Republic'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series identified its species as exogorths.<ref name="kotor18" />

The space-slug scene in ''Empire'' was drawn from the mythological motif<ref name="dvd">''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' [[Star Wars home video releases#Star_Wars_Trilogy_DVD_set|DVD]] commentary</ref> of [[Wikipedia:Jonah|Jonah and the Whale]], an archetypal story of journeying into the belly of the beast.<ref name="magic of myth" /> Artists [[Ralph McQuarrie]] and [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]] developed the space slug in sketches.<ref name="db" />

For filming, the slug was realized as a puppet seventy-nine centimeters in length and twenty-eight in diameter.<ref name="db" /> The puppet was covered with an exterior designed by visual effects supervisor [[Phil Tippett]] and was operated by special effects artist [[Jon Berg]] for more than fifty takes over a period of one week. The space slug was a heavy puppet whose jaws were closed by a return spring mechanism.<ref name="Cinefex">{{BookCite|title=[[Wikipedia:Cinefex|''Cinefex'']]|number=Issue 3}}</ref> Night-shift camera operators shot gag footage involving an alternate space-slug puppet made out of a sock.<ref name="laserdisc">''[[Star Wars Trilogy: The Definitive Collection]]''</ref>

[[Industrial Light & Magic]] chief model maker [[Lorne Peterson]] created a four-and-a-half-foot-long model of the creature's hinged jaws for the shot of the ''Millennium Falcon'' racing out of the asteroid tunnel, casting the five-inch-tall teeth from a plastic [[Wikipedia:Urethane|urethane]] that possessed a translucent [[Wikipedia:Ivory|ivory]] quality. Additional teeth were later given as gifts to celebrities or industry guests to the model shop.<ref name="sculpting">''[[Sculpting a Galaxy: Inside the Star Wars Model Shop]]''</ref> The set of the interior of the space slug was created by the laying of black [[Wikipedia:Visqueen|Visqueen]] plastic on the floor of the [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] set, draping black curtains around the ''Millennium Falcon'', and releasing a fog of dry ice. Visual effects supervisor [[John Knoll]] called it "undoubtedly the least expensive set built" for the film.<ref name="365Days">''[[Creating the Worlds of Star Wars: 365 Days]]''</ref> To create the sound and feeling of slime when the film's characters were walking on the slug's tongue, Foley editors [[Scott Hecker]] and [[Robert R. Rutledge]] used nearly twenty-five pounds of pure beef fat in large slabs, as well as dozens of raw eggs, which they then walked on with various pieces of footwear to create the sounds of the characters' footsteps.<ref name="chronicles">{{SWArchive|url=movies/episode-v/chronicles20100325.html|text=''Empire'' Chronicles: Space Slug}}</ref>

[[File:Thejawsthatbite.jpg|thumb|left|275px|Industrial Light & Magic chief model maker Lorne Peterson examines his model of the space slug's jaws.]]
Although ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] was unhappy with the final scene of the ''Falcon'' flying away from the creature's gaping maw, asserting that it worked better on paper,<ref name="dvd" /> [[Lucasfilm]] internet content developer [[Pete Vilmur]] has called the space slug one of the most memorable life forms introduced in the film.<ref name="chronicles" /> Author Lukas Kendall has praised composer [[John Williams]]'s scoring of the scene, describing what he calls "a wonderful creepiness and atmosphere with just the subtle effects of the ship, a brilliant use of sound."<ref name="filmscore">{{BookCite|title=[[Wikipedia:Film Score Monthly|''Film Score Monthly'']]|date=[[January]]/[[February]] [[1997]]}}</ref>

When author [[John Jackson Miller]] was pitching ideas for his ''Knights of the Old Republic'' comic series in [[2005]], he conceived of a centerpiece for [[2007|the second year]] of the series being something biological, spaceborne, and big, invoking the "[[Wikipedia:Here be dragons|Here be dragons]]" feeling of old maps while being something more than just a large gun. As he began writing the story arc, he grew cautious of introducing a large, interstellar life form that would violate the ground rules of the ''Star Wars'' universe, but, after watching a repeat of ''Empire'', realized that the space slug was relatively unexplored and not properly named within the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]; previous material had identified it as being a relic of the ancient world, and Miller's comic series took place [[3963 BBY|nearly 4,000 years]] prior to the events of ''Empire''.<ref name="18prod">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknights/swkotor18.html|text=''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #18''}}</ref> The species was dubbed "exorgorth,"<ref name="19prod">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknights/swkotor19.html|text=''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #19''}}</ref> and artist [[Brian Ching]] designed a visual look for the creatures that, along with the name, was inspired by the works of author [[Wikipedia:H.P. Lovecraft|H.P. Lovecraft]].<ref name="18prod" /><ref name="dhboards">{{DHBoards|url=viewtopic.php?t=11859|thread=KotOR #18 -- Here there be dragons!|user=[[John Jackson Miller]]|time=7:31 AM}}</ref> The name was misspelled "exogorth" on one occasion during the lettering stage of issue 18, and, after catching the mistake too late, Miller decided to make it the official spelling. Despite this, "exorgorth" appears several times within the issue.<ref name="19prod" />
